title: Uptown versus downtown entertainment and gambling
summary: The Irish Channel had warehouses and gambling clubs; piano joints were downtown on Rampart Street.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Did it seem very different down here? The music was the same band?

Well, that's in the olden time. You know how first, see? They don't do the things. They didn't have much sport. We used to always have to come back for such things as dances and things. We all had to come back at that time. We all had to come back at that time for everything. It was nothing out there but a lot of work, warehouses, big drays, different drays out there. And people scattered about. In my days there was a lot of gambling. There was a lot of gambling. In other words you could, they'd give you a charter to gamble. There was a lot of gambling clubs out there. Most people would go out there because they had plenty of money. See? But there were back down here where they had all the, but I don't know what you all call them. Places where they had the piano, the drum, and the horn. Well, that was all across Ramport Street. You had to get the Ramport Street to catch all that. You mean the tongue. That's right. And that was all back this way. And out of my way, well, we had one or two of them scattered about there. We had one at Diamond and South Peter. Well, we had a piano and one show back on Saturday and Sunday. You know, but most of the idiots out there was gambling. We've been gambling, that's all.
